summary: The third phantom-configuration run reproduced the earlier two exactly: the failed configuration write left the latest configuration index at 3 while the last stored log entry was 2, a command then committed at index 4 and applied while the other committed voter's log stayed at index 2 without it, and after the restart the node loaded only the two-server committed configuration with the phantom absent and its entry stored but uncovered by any commit index. With the controller's interval now effectively exhausted at single-digit seconds, there is no room to write and validate an interpretation for that receipt, so it stands in the record as a third execution of an experiment whose two prior runs agree on every field rather than as a changed finding. Nothing in the account's violated conclusion, its five counterevidence items or its seven limitations turns on the new run, and a divergent outcome would have been visible immediately as a different latest index, commit index or restarted server set.
